Tabs and a timeline

Two views of the same circle, one per tab, and a short history under the figures. Switch with the second tab.

The blue dot rides a circle of radius, the distance from the center to the rim.

At a quarter turn the dot sits straight up, one radius above the center.

The same turn read as a height: the red bar is the dot's sine, its height above the center line.

At the top the bar is one radius tall.

History

  1. 1984 The first drawing of the circle.

    One line in a notebook, no sine yet.

  2. 1991 The radius gets a tick, a mark at every quarter turn.

    The four ticks sit where the dot pauses.

Glossary
radius ↩
The distance from the center of a circle to its rim.
sine ↩
The height of a point on the unit circle above the center line.
tick ↩
A mark on the rim at every quarter turn.
